primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease secondary to diabetic nephropathy
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) & NICE NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily (morning); titrate to 5 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated, max 10 mg daily
medications.purpose: Renoprotective and antihypertensive (proteinuria >30 mg/mmol and hypertension)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: ACE‑I recommended for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid panel at 3‑6 months then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD with IHD, diabetes and hyperlipidaemia
medications.nice_justification: NG203: All CKD patients should receive a statin as CV risk equivalent

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (adjust up to 40 mg BID based on volume status and BP)
medications.duration: Ongoing while volume overloaded or BP >130/80 mmHg – review after 2 weeks and then each visit
medications.purpose: Control volume overload and assist BP control (thiazides ineffective at eGFR ≈10 mL/min)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Loop diuretics recommended for hypertension/volume control in CKD stage 4

medications.medication: Insulin glargine (Basal) + rapid‑acting insulin as needed
medications.dose: Insulin glargine 10 U subcutaneously nightly; rapid‑acting insulin dose individualized per carbohydrate counting and glucose monitoring
medications.duration: Lifelong – glucose review weekly for first month, then quarterly
medications.nice_justification: NG203 & NG107: Insulin is preferred glucose‑lowering agent in advanced CKD; avoid oral agents cleared renally

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for altered potassium balance (hyperkalaemia from ACE‑I, hypokalaemia from loop diuretic) and AKI if volume depleted
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and creatinine 1–2 weeks after initiation and after any dose change; ensure euvolemia
No dose adjustment needed; monitor liver function as per statin safety

interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I may improve insulin sensitivity, modest risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on hypoglycaemia symptoms; consider small insulin dose reduction if fasting glucose falls below target

contraindications.reason: eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
Accelerate CKD progression and increase AKI risk in stage 4 CKD
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
Risk of hyperkalaemia with ACE‑I therapy and reduced renal excretion
contraindications.alternative: Avoid potassium supplementation unless hypokalaemia documented

contraindications.reason: NICE TA775 indicates use only for eGFR ≥20 mL/min; patient eGFR ≈10 mL/min
contraindications.alternative: Not indicated; focus on ACE‑I, statin, insulin, and volume control

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium not available – must be measured before and after starting Ramipril
Liver function tests not available – required before initiating Atorvastatin
Current blood pressure reading not recorded – needed to confirm hypertension and titrate antihypertensives
HbA1c and fasting glucose not available – required to individualise insulin dosing
Calcium, phosphate, PTH, bicarbonate not measured – needed before adding vitamin D analogues, phosphate binders, or sodium bicarbonate
Allergy history not documented – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or insulin allergies before prescribing
treatment_summary: Start renoprotective ACE‑inhibitor (Ramipril) and cardiovascular risk‑reduction statin (Atorvastatin) per NG203. Add a low‑dose loop diuretic (Furosemide) if volume overload or uncontrolled BP. Replace metformin with basal‑bolus insulin regimen for diabetes control, as insulin is the recommended agent in CKD stage 4. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, blood pressure, and glucose closely, and adjust doses according to response. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, ACE‑I/ARB combo, potassium supplements, and SGLT2 inhibitors. Further CKD‑MBD management (vitamin D, phosphate binders, ESA) will be considered after relevant labs are obtained.
